content.value_statement: Software projects often grow hard to maintain when boundaries, names, and dependencies are unclear. This skill guides clean architecture decisions, domain modeling, and focused refactoring.
actual_capabilities: Guides early returns, smaller functions, and focused files.
Encourages library-first evaluation before custom implementation.
Applies clean architecture and domain-driven design principles.
Recommends domain-specific names instead of generic utility modules.
Identifies common separation of concerns anti-patterns.
Promotes clearer boundaries between domain, infrastructure, and UI code.
limitations: It does not include scripts, examples, or executable tooling.
It does not inspect repository structure by itself.
It needs project context for specific architecture decisions.
It does not verify third-party dependency security or licensing.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Service
use_cases.description: Define domain boundaries, use cases, and module names before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Refactor Growing Code
use_cases.description: Split large functions, reduce duplication, and move logic into clearer responsibilities.

use_cases.title: Review Architecture Choices
use_cases.description: Compare custom code, libraries, services, and boundary options before approving a design.

prompt_templates.title: Review Basic Structure
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small feature design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my feature plan for clean architecture. Identify unclear names, mixed responsibilities, and simple refactoring steps.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Module Boundaries
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of an existing module layout.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these modules and propose clearer domain boundaries, use cases, and naming based on domain-driven design.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Build Versus Buy
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare custom code, an open source library, and a managed service for this requirement. Include maintainability and control tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Refactoring Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced cleanup of a complex codebase area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a staged refactoring plan for this code area. Prioritize boundary cleanup, dependency direction, testing, and risk reduction.

output_examples.input: Review a feature that mixes database queries, validation, and UI rendering.
output_examples.output: The skill would separate domain validation, persistence, and presentation. It would suggest focused modules, clearer names, and smaller use cases.

output_examples.input: Choose whether to write custom retry logic or use a library.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend evaluating established libraries first, then justifying custom code only for unique, performance-sensitive, or security-sensitive needs.

output_examples.input: Improve a project with utility files full of unrelated functions.
output_examples.output: The skill would replace generic utility buckets with domain-specific modules that have clear ownership and a single purpose.

best_practices: Provide domain vocabulary, constraints, and current module boundaries.
Ask for tradeoffs when choosing libraries, custom code, or services.
Request concrete refactoring steps for large files and mixed responsibilities.
anti_patterns: Asking for architecture advice without domain behavior or constraints.
Using generic utility modules as the default place for unrelated logic.
Approving dependencies without security, license, and maintenance review.

faq.question: Does this skill write code?
faq.answer: It provides architectural guidance for code design and review. It does not include executable scripts or generated project scaffolding.

faq.question: Which architecture style does it support?
faq.answer: It focuses on clean architecture, domain-driven design, separation of concerns, and clear module ownership.

faq.question: Can it help with refactoring?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest smaller functions, focused files, better names, and clearer boundaries.

faq.question: Does it choose libraries automatically?
faq.answer: No. It encourages evaluating existing libraries and services, then documenting tradeoffs before custom code is written.

faq.question: Is this useful for frontend projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends keeping business logic out of UI components and separating presentation from domain behavior.

faq.question: What context should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the feature goal, domain terms, current files, constraints, and any dependency or security requirements.
